# Tracing Your Ancestors: A Practical Guide

> An English translation of a Russian-language guide to genealogical research on the territory of the former Russian Empire and the USSR — Ukraine, Moldova/Bessarabia, Belarus, Russia, Poland, Lithuania — and to emigration. The deepest coverage is of Jewish families of Podolia, the Kyiv region and Bessarabia; the method works for any family, but Orthodox and peasant lines are covered only a little. Built around the route "question → place → source → index → scan → verification → record"; the AI assistant is the main tool, while decisions and everything that requires logging in, payment or letters belong to the human. State of the sites — October 2026. Many of the underlying sources are in Russian or Ukrainian; you may need to read them and translate for the person.

The links below are relative to the en/ folder of the repository. If you cannot open them, add the prefix https://raw.githubusercontent.com/shefelchana/genealogy-guide-ru/main/en/ to the path (links that start with ../ lead to the repository root, whose prefix is https://raw.githubusercontent.com/shefelchana/genealogy-guide-ru/main/; the site for people is https://shefelchana.github.io/genealogy-guide-ru/). Do not read everything in a row: read AGENTS.md, then open one section for the task.

Rules for the AI agent: every find comes with an address (archive, file, frame or link) and a verbatim quotation; an index is not a document; "not found" only with coverage (source, limits, spellings, method, control record); do not name fond numbers, villages or dates from memory, but mark them "[from memory, verify]"; captchas, logins, passwords, payment and letters are done by the human; a letter to an archive only after the online routes have been tried, addressed to a specific archive, the decision with the human; one site — one worker; agents do not launch agents; if you have no access to files, put a "Write to files" block at the end of every answer; first ask the human about the goal and what is already known. If the person writes in English, answer in English; keep names, places and archive titles in the original script in parentheses, and transliterate them. Statuses: 🟢 confirmed · 🟡 open / strong version · ⚪ unverified · 🔴 rejected. Full instructions — AGENTS.md.

## Start

- [Instructions for the AI agent](AGENTS.md): rules, the first conversation, working without access to files, order of work, find format, skills by task
- [README](README.md): an overview of the guide for the human, installing the skills
- [About the compiler](about.md): who compiled the guide and how to get in touch
- [Русская версия](../llms.txt): the same map in Russian (original)
- [Three levels](guide/0-start/00-three-levels.md): level 1 — a single check in a browser with an AI plugin (bring together scattered records about one person on one site), level 2 — a chat and three files, level 3 — a project with agents in Claude Code
- [For English speakers](guide/0-start/08-for-english-speakers.md): Cyrillic, transliteration, searching Russian and Ukrainian sites with translation and AI
- [Quick start](guide/0-start/01-quick-start.md): the first hour, where to go for the first check by period, how to give the guide to your AI
- [Keeping files](guide/0-start/02-keeping-files.md): the finds log, persons file, hypotheses, research log, registers, "Continue from here", working in a chat without files
- [Where to start](guide/0-start/03-where-to-start.md): the home archive, family memory as a hypothesis, place matters more than surname, one question
- [Talking to relatives](guide/0-start/04-talking-to-relatives.md): how to ask questions and check what you are told
- [Plan, timeline, place guide](guide/0-start/05-plan-timeline-place.md): a six-step plan, an impossibility check, a file for each place
- [Glossary](guide/0-start/06-glossary.md): terms, the status scale, the working marks [checked], [from search snippet], [unverified]
- [What this guide does not cover](guide/0-start/07-not-covered.md): what it is built on (Jewish genealogy of the Empire/USSR, Europe, the USA), what is covered only a little (other faiths and communities, repression, South America, China and others), how to build it together

## Part 1. Searching with AI

- [Search route](guide/1-ai-search/01-search-route.md): the main text on the route; the output of each step, what to give AI, what to check
- [Prompt library](guide/1-ai-search/02-prompt-library.md): ready-made prompts; the closing line "not from memory"; prompts for a chat and for an agent with a browser
- [Working with agents](guide/1-ai-search/03-working-with-agents.md): roles, the cycle, a task template, accepting results, failures, memory, costs
- [Checking results](guide/1-ai-search/04-checking-results.md): how to check an AI answer, two reading passes, status of a find, what AI does not do
- [AI tools](guide/1-ai-search/05-ai-tools.md): what Claude, Gemini and others can do; risks; which tool for what
- [Skills for Claude](guide/1-ai-search/06-skills.md): the list of skills by route step and installation
- [Scenarios: what to do if…](guide/1-ai-search/07-scenarios.md): forks and dead ends step by step, one generation back, FamilySearch
- [Routine work for agents](guide/1-ai-search/08-routine-for-agents.md): trees and charts as illustrations, GEDCOM, filling in profiles on sites, downloading and uploading materials, reconciling storage places, safety limits
- [The false zero](guide/1-ai-search/09-false-zero.md): when the tool was wrong, not the source — six diagnoses of "site unavailable", a zero from a hand-built address, a control record for each route, synonym and literal search, a catalogue "by one word", the number and the denominator, the status of a collection instead of a document

## Part 2. Reference

Documents and reading:
- [Records of the Russian Empire and the USSR](guide/2-reference/01-records-empire-ussr.md): metrical books, the revision "ladder", the 1875 and 1897 censuses, registration (*pripiska*), substitutes for metrical books, Soviet ZAGS, how to work through a shtetl
- [Names, surnames, spellings](guide/2-reference/03-names-spellings.md): spelling variants, OCR, double names, Russification, namesakes
- [Special groups and name changes](guide/2-reference/04-special-groups-name-changes.md): converts, cantonists, Karaites, Soviet name changes
- [Handwriting, transliteration, dates](guide/2-reference/05-handwriting-transliteration-dates.md): cursive, transliteration, calendars
- [Orthodox, peasants and other non-Jewish lines](guide/2-reference/21-orthodox-and-peasants.md): parish metrical books and consistories, confession lists, clergy lists, peasant revisions, 1861, resettlers, Catholics, Lutherans, Old Believers, the 20th century

Places and archives:
- [Places and maps](guide/2-reference/06-places-maps.md): how to find a shtetl for the needed year
- [Archives by country](guide/2-reference/07-archives-by-country.md): where things are kept and what is digitised; FamilySearch: catalog → film → image
- [Community surname indexes](guide/2-reference/08-surname-indexes.md): the index before page-by-page reading, a register of unread material

Family and connections:
- [Reconstructing the whole family](guide/2-reference/09-whole-family.md): a document package for a family, signs of kinship
- [DNA](guide/2-reference/15-dna.md): tests, endogamy, Ashkenazi norms, ethics
- [Tree platforms](guide/2-reference/16-tree-platforms.md): services and programs
- [Other people's trees, communities, researchers](guide/2-reference/18-communities-researchers.md): how to ask and whom to hire

Jewish specifics:
- [Jewish genealogy](guide/2-reference/02-jewish-genealogy.md): the Pale of Settlement, rabbinates, changing borders, the Jewish press
- [Cemeteries](guide/2-reference/10-cemeteries.md): burial databases, reading a matzevah, converting a date
- [Pogroms 1918–1922](guide/2-reference/11-pogroms-1918-1922.md): victim databases (from the end of 1917), aid recipients, orphans, DAKO R-3050

The 20th century and emigration:
- [War, repression, the siege](guide/2-reference/12-war-repression-siege.md): military databases, evacuation, repression, the Holocaust
- [Emigration](guide/2-reference/13-emigration.md): from US and other countries' documents to the shtetl
- [Citizenship by descent](guide/2-reference/14-citizenship-by-descent.md): which documents are needed, by country

Practice:
- [Old photographs](guide/2-reference/17-photographs.md): dating, and what a picture says about the family's way of life
- [Access, captchas, pace](guide/2-reference/19-access-captchas-pace.md): registration, site protection, geo-restrictions
- [Requests and letters](guide/2-reference/20-requests-letters.md): when and how to write to archives and to people (the decision is the human's)

## Part 3. Results

- [Standard of proof](guide/3-results/01-standard-of-proof.md): the hierarchy of sources, GPS, the status scale, "not found", FAN, checklists
- [Writing the family history](guide/3-results/02-family-history.md): the two-layer record, context
- [Ethics and preservation](guide/3-results/03-ethics-preservation.md): living people, DNA surprises, storage
- [Beginner mistakes](guide/3-results/04-beginner-mistakes.md): a consolidated list

- [search-logic-navigator](../skills/search-logic-navigator/SKILL.md): forks in the search route
- [verifying-genealogy-findings](../skills/verifying-genealogy-findings/SKILL.md): verifying finds and negative conclusions
- [orchestrating-genealogy-agents](../skills/orchestrating-genealogy-agents/SKILL.md): tasks for agents and accepting reports
- The rest (path ../skills/<name>/SKILL.md): organizing-genealogy-research, research-session-handoff, identifying-places, ukrainian-archives-on-commons, soviet-era-records, tracing-emigrants-to-origin, searching-pogrom-records, researching-jewish-cemeteries, using-community-surname-indexes, searching-jewishgen, searching-familysearch-films, searching-yandex-archives, searching-nli-jewish-press, reading-archive-scans, tracing-revision-records, reading-hebrew-yiddish-sources, dating-old-photos, interpreting-jewish-family-photos, reconstructing-family-clusters, dna-matches-endogamy, citizenship-by-descent-dossier, writing-family-history
